title: The temple turned
hookLine: turned away from a temple for his low caste, Namdev sang, and the hymn says the temple turned to face him (Malar, Namdev)

cards: Laughing, playing, a man walks up to a temple to sing. Before he gets far, someone grabs him and hauls him out. The reason is his family: he's a printer of cloth, and the ones who throw him out count that as low.
He picks up his blanket, walks around to the back of the building, and sits down by the rear wall. It could end there. In Namdev's own hymn, it's only getting started.

teach.b: The hymn is in Raag Malar, on Ang 1292. In paraphrase, Namdev says: laughing and playing, I came to your temple. While I was worshipping, I was seized and thrown out.
Low is my caste, O Lord.

teach.h: WHY WAS I BORN A PRINTER?
teach.b: Why was I born a printer of cloth? I picked up my blanket and went back, and sat behind the temple. And then the turn.
As Namdev sang the Lord's praises, the temple turned around to face the devotee. Hear the question in the middle. Why was I born a printer?
It's honest, the hurt of a man shut out for something he never chose, and the hymn doesn't pretend it didn't sting. Then look at what he does with it. He doesn't break the door down.

teach.h: HE SITS AT THE BACK AND SINGS.
teach.b: He sits at the back wall and keeps praising, and in the hymn, the building moves to him. Notice who the hymn follows. The ones who threw him out get one line and then drop out of it.
Everything after is a man singing and a Lord who listens.

teach.h: THE ONE THROWN OUT, AT THE FRONT.
teach.b: The building that had its back to him ends up facing him, and the one who was thrown out is now the one at the front.
This ends our week, and it's the plainest picture of it: low, honest, and received.

how: Sikhs sing Namdev's Malar hymn as gurbani and often tell the turning of the temple when speaking about the Gurus' rejection of caste, which gurdwaras express in langar, where everyone sits and eats together.

games.q: you've just been thrown out of the temple for your caste. what do you do?
o: shout at the men at the door.
walk home and never sing again.
sit behind the temple and keep singing.
games.why: Namdev picked up his blanket, sat at the back wall and sang, and the hymn says the temple turned to face him.

practice: Bring to mind a person at the edge of your circle: the quiet coworker nobody invites, the relative who doesn't get the call, the neighbor who eats alone.
Hold their face for a few breaths, turning toward them the way the temple turned to face Namdev. If you pray, you can say Waheguru with their name.

wordCard.voice: Dehura. The temple in Namdev's hymn, which turned to face him after he was thrown out and sat singing at the back wall.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: dehura, a temple, the building that turns in Namdev's hymn.

carryVoice: Your line: low, honest, and received. The back wall can become the front. That's the week.
